paragraphs: An atmospheric diving suit is a submarine shaped like a person. The occupant stays at surface pressure inside it, which means no decompression and no gas mixture to calculate, and the rotary joints that let the arms and legs move under crushing pressure are the entire engineering achievement.

The model holds 157,238 polygons and 166,021 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification, and rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Cinema 4D and Maya.
At $119 it suits underwater and marine visualisation, documentary and education work, offshore and salvage presentation, film, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A basket with something in it is the difference between a shop and a shop that is open. Retail renders live or die on that kind of detail: the trolley left mid aisle, the basket with a few items, the evidence that people have been here.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying baskets together with goods as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $119 the set suits retail and supermarket visualisation, packaging and product presentation, advertising, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

Taking a vehicle apart is how anybody actually learns what is in one. Body panels, glass, running gear and interior separated from each other, with the frame removed, gives an exploded view that a cutaway drawing can only approximate.

The model holds 289,836 polygons and 143,521 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in the disassembled state without the frame. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $109 it suits automotive engineering visualisation, technical and training material, parts catalogues and manufacturing presentation, education and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The cooling tower is not the reactor, and almost every photograph of nuclear power gets that wrong. It is a heat exchanger, the same one a coal plant would use, and the reactor itself is the far less photogenic containment building beside it.

The scene holds 248,436 polygons and 257,888 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 21 maps, 6 at 8192x8192 and 15 at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $109 it suits energy and infrastructure visualisation, education and documentary work, news graphics, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

Lights on is a specific design decision for an air taxi. A vehicle that flies over a city at night has to be legible from the ground and reassuring from inside, so the lighting is treated as branding rather than as a regulation to satisfy.
The model holds 175,104 polygons and 90,275 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with a simple interior and the lights on. It carries StemCell certification.
At $99 it suits future mobility visualisation, technology and transport presentation, advertising, science fiction film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The largest submarines ever built carry two pressure hulls side by side inside one outer casing, with the missile tubes between them and forward of the sail. The Russians called the class Akula, meaning shark; NATO called it Typhoon, and the second name is the one that stuck in the west.

The model holds 426,868 polygons and 228,579 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Maya and Cinema 4D.
At $99 it suits naval and defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film and television, and game environments. On sale since 2023.

Football kit is armour with a jersey pulled over it. The shoulder pads define the silhouette, the helmet is a certified piece of safety equipment rather than a hat, and the whole outfit exists because the sport was killing people until it was mandated.
The uniform holds 66,530 polygons and 66,755 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 22 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $99 it suits sports visualisation and broadcast graphics, equipment and apparel marketing, game characters, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The DB9 is the car that saved the shape of the modern Aston Martin. Every model since has been an argument about its proportions, and the design is old enough now to be judged rather than marketed, which is usually when a car either becomes a classic or does not.

The model is dense at 713,865 polygons and 429,787 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with a simple interior. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a blue build is offered separately.
At $99 it suits automotive marketing and configurators, street and architectural scenes, advertising, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A bakery sells by sight, and the display case is the whole shop. Loaves stacked to show the crust, pastries at eye level, and the arrangement changing through the day as things sell out: it is merchandising older than the word.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying display pieces as static items. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $99 the set suits retail and hospitality visualisation, food and product marketing, interior and architectural scenes, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2017.

Packaging is where a bakery stops being a kitchen and becomes a factory. The machine has to handle something soft, warm and irregular at a rate no person could match, without crushing it, which is a harder problem than it sounds and why these lines look so over engineered.
The model holds 310,658 polygons and 316,662 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 10 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $99 it suits food industry and manufacturing visualisation, equipment marketing, training material, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2019.

The Starliner is a capsule designed to be reused and to land on ground rather than water, which is unusual for an American spacecraft. With the hatch open it stops being a sealed object and becomes something a crew climbs into, which is a more useful image for most work.

The model is light at 53,814 polygons and 56,375 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the airlock open. It is built to CheckMate specification, and the library also holds the closed capsule and a transport configuration.
At $99 it suits space programme visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and education work, film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The Capitol Records building is usually described as a stack of records with a stylus on top, which the architect always denied. Either way it was the first circular office tower in the world, and the shape came from a practical argument about daylight rather than from vinyl.
The model holds 332,446 polygons and 367,085 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in white. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, music industry and cultural imagery, city skyline scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A flatbed carries what will not fit in a box: machinery, steel, anything awkward. The deck is the entire product, and the tractor in front of it is chosen for how much it can pull rather than for how it looks.

This is the simplified build, 520,373 polygons and 548,029 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, in black, intended for scenes where the vehicle is not the focus. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits logistics and haulage visualisation, fleet mockups, industrial and street scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Cassie has no upper body at all, which is the point: a pair of legs built to prove that dynamic balance can be solved on its own. The knees bend backwards like a bird's, because the researchers took the design from ostriches rather than from people.

The model holds 175,436 polygons and 181,320 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in blue, and comes rigged for posing or animation. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and native rigged builds for Cinema 4D and Maya are offered separately.
At $99 it suits robotics and technology visualisation, research and education material, advertising, science fiction film, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
